summary: Russia launched a massive combined missile and drone strike overnight targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure nationwide, hitting thermal power plants in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih, Ladizhyn, and Kharkiv, causing widespread blackouts affecting over 200,000 consumers in Dnipro alone. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted numerous Kh-101 cruise missiles and jet drones, while Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers rearmed at Engels airbase for potential follow-on strikes. Ukraine struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery, one of Russia's largest, and may receive 500 PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot systems under a U.S. State Department approval.
key_points: Russia fired over 70 Kh-101 cruise missiles in multiple waves at thermal power plants and substations across Ukraine overnight. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77898)
Ukrainian forces attacked the Yaroslavl oil refinery, a top-five Russian facility supplying fuel to Moscow and the defense industry. (Source: @UkraineNow/85091)
Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers landed at Engels airbase to reload cruise missiles before returning to Far Eastern bases. (Source: @eRadarrua/128383)
A Russian hospital strike in Kharkiv injured 73 people and forced evacuation of over 200 patients. (Source: @UkraineNow/85087)
Follow-up aerial bombs on a shelter in Komyshuvakha killed 18 civilians. (Source: @UkraineNow/85080)
Ukraine established an electronic warfare dome over Kyiv that disrupted Shahed drone navigation. (Source: @UkraineNow/85084)
U.S. State Department approved potential sale of 500 PAC-3 interceptors for Ukrainian Patriot systems. (Source: @UkraineNow/85077)
Russia-Ukraine working-level talks scheduled for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi with U.S. mediation. (Source: @UkraineNow/85086)

sections.executive_summary: Russia launched a massive combined missile and drone strike overnight targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure nationwide, hitting thermal power plants in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih, Ladizhyn, and Kharkiv, causing widespread blackouts affecting over 200,000 consumers in Dnipro alone. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted numerous Kh-101 cruise missiles and jet drones, while Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers rearmed at Engels airbase for potential follow-on strikes. Ukraine struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery, one of Russia's largest, and may receive 500 PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot systems under a U.S. State Department approval.

points: Ukraine's defense forces attacked the Yaroslavl oil refinery, one of Russia's top five refineries producing gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuel for the Moscow region and Russian defense industry. (Source: @UkraineNow/85091)

Kyiv established an electronic warfare dome to counter Shahed drones, involving the General Staff, Defense Ministry, Interior Ministry, NSDC, and OPU, forcing Russia to pause and modernize drones. (Source: @UkraineNow/85084)
Ukraine may receive 500 PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot systems after U.S. State Department approved a possible sale on October 30. (Source: @UkraineNow/85077)
Ukraine agreed to pause strikes on Russian refineries at U.S. request but resumed after continued Russian attacks, hitting three refineries in recent days. (Source: @UkraineNow/85074)

Four National Guard servicemen were detained after a violent incident in Petropavlivska Borshchahivka, Kyiv region; Kyrylo Budanov arrived on scene as shootings continued and a crowd damaged a city bus. (Source: @UkraineNow/85083)
Russia-Ukraine working-level negotiations are scheduled for November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi with U.S. mediation, per Witkoff. (Source: @UkraineNow/85086)

Russia conducted a massive combined overnight strike using ballistic and cruise missiles, jet and conventional Shahed drones, and KAB guided bombs against dozens of Ukrainian cities, focusing on energy infrastructure. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77898)

Russian forces launched dozens of Kh-101 cruise missiles at targets including Ladizhynska TES (Vinnytsia), Prydniprovska TES (Dnipro), Kryvorizka TES, and Zmiivska TES (Kharkiv), with over 200,000 consumers losing power in Dnipro. (Source: @UkraineNow/85085, @eRadarrua/128369)

Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS strategic bombers landed at Engels airbase for reloading with cruise missiles before returning to Far Eastern bases, while other bombers returned to Olenya and Ukrainka airfields. (Source: @eRadarrua/128383)
Russia officially withdrew from the European Convention for the Prevention of Torture, ending independent international monitoring of detention facilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/85072)
The Kremlin stated Russia does not plan new "humanitarian operations" similar to Oleshky, per Peskov. (Source: @UkraineNow/85075)
A significant ballistic missile stockpile remains in Bryansk and was not used overnight; threat of strikes on Kyiv persists for the next 2-3 days. (Source: @eRadarrua/128378)
Russian forces struck a hospital in Kharkiv, injuring 73 people and forcing evacuation of over 200 patients to other medical facilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/85087)
Zmiivska thermal power plant in Kharkiv region was targeted, causing critical heating and hot water outages across the city. (Source: @UkraineNow/85085)
Russian aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha, killing 18 people after a follow-up strike of nine bombs on a shelter where civilians had taken cover. (Source: @UkraineNow/85080)
A residential high-rise in Dnipro was hit during the overnight attack, causing casualties. (Source: @eRadarrua/128361)

Multiple jet drones launched from Bryansk region transited northern Chernihiv region toward Kyiv, with at least four drones passing near Berezna en route to the capital. (Source: @kpszsu/92752, @eRadarrua/128372)
Jet drones crossed the Chornobyl exclusion zone from Chernihiv region into Kyiv region, with one drone detected near Kaniv, Cherkasy region. (Source: @kpszsu/92748, @kpszsu/92765)
Russian cruise missiles and drones targeted energy infrastructure in Chernihiv region, including substations, as part of the nationwide attack. (Source: @UkraineNow/85085)
Air defense units tracked jet drones over Zhytomyr region moving toward Kyiv, with detections near Korostyshiv, Korosten, and Narodychi. (Source: @eRadarrua/128376)
Jet drones launched from the Black Sea targeted Odesa region, with one drone heading toward Ochakiv and another toward Sarata/Artsyz near the Danube. (Source: @kpszsu/92758, @kpszsu/92772)
Russian drones attacked energy substations in Odesa region, causing local power outages from debris impacts and direct hits on grid elements. (Source: @UkraineNow/85085)
A jet drone from Mykolaiv region flew toward Kryve Ozero, while another transited Voronivka toward Vinnytsia region. (Source: @kpszsu/92746, @kpszsu/92781)
Russian forces struck port and energy infrastructure in Odesa region, with debris damaging distribution network components. (Source: @eRadarrua/128369)

Overnight, Russia fired over 70 Kh-101 cruise missiles in multiple waves, including 30 missiles toward Vinnytsia region, 20 toward Ladizhyn, 11 at Dnipro, and 7 at Ladizhynska TES, with additional missiles targeting Poltava, Kryvyi Rih, and Khmelnytskyi regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77884, @mon1tor_ua/77888, @mon1tor_ua/77879, @mon1tor_ua/77890, @mon1tor_ua/77860, @mon1tor_ua/77862)

Massive Shahed drone swarms accompanied the missile strike, targeting substations in Dnipropetrovsk, Odesa, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kyiv, and Chernivtsi regions, prompting emergency power restrictions nationwide. (Source: @UkraineNow/85085)

Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers launched cruise missiles from Caspian and far eastern sectors, with at least two aircraft confirmed landing at Engels for reloading before returning to distant bases. (Source: @eRadarrua/128383, @eRadarrua/128370)
Ukrainian air defense created an electronic warfare dome over Kyiv that temporarily neutralized Shahed drones, forcing Russian modifications to drone guidance systems. (Source: @UkraineNow/85084)
Ballistic missile threat to Kyiv remains high with unused stockpiles in Bryansk; analysts expect strikes on the capital within 2-3 days. (Source: @eRadarrua/128378)

Jet drones (reactive UAVs) were detected across northern, central, and southern Ukraine, entering from Belarus, Bryansk, and the Black Sea, targeting Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kirovohrad, and Odesa regions. (Source: @kpszsu/92745, @kpszsu/92748, @kpszsu/92752, @kpszsu/92758, @kpszsu/92769, @kpszsu/92772, @kpszsu/92773, @kpszsu/92781, @eRadarrua/128376, @eRadarrua/128384)

key_developments: Russia launched a massive combined strike overnight Nov 2-3 with 70+ Kh-101 cruise missiles, Shahed drones, and jet UAVs targeting thermal power plants in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih, Ladizhyn, and Kharkiv, cutting power to 200k+ consumers in Dnipro alone. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/77898, @UkraineNow/85085)

Ukrainian forces struck the Yaroslavl oil refinery, a top-five Russian facility supplying fuel to Moscow and the defense industry, marking a significant deep-strike capability. (Source: @UkraineNow/85091)
Russian Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers rearmed at Engels airbase after initial sorties, indicating preparation for sustained long-range aviation strikes in coming days. (Source: @eRadarrua/128383)

A Russian hospital strike in Kharkiv injured 73 and forced evacuation of 200+ patients, while a follow-up aerial bomb attack on a shelter in Komyshuvakha killed 18 civilians. (Source: @UkraineNow/85087, @UkraineNow/85080)
Ukraine established an electronic warfare dome over Kyiv that disrupted Shahed navigation, forcing Russia to pause and modify drone guidance systems. (Source: @UkraineNow/85084)
U.S. State Department approved potential sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE interceptors for Ukrainian Patriot systems, significantly boosting air defense capacity if delivered. (Source: @UkraineNow/85077)

Russia-Ukraine working-level talks set for Nov 10-11 in Abu Dhabi with U.S. mediation, while Poland launched a border security operation with Kaliningrad over sabotage threats. (Source: @UkraineNow/85086, @UkraineNow/85076)
